# Introduction

In the [last article](https://biscotty.net/posts/data-science/r-census/abq-demographics) I looked at age, race, and educational attainment in Albuquerque, with a particular focus on differences between council districts. In some cases, the variation was striking. In particular, the third district seemed quite different from the others in a number of ways. Now I would like to apply some statistical testing to see if this impression is valid.

# Setup

I will begin by loading the required libraries, as well as the datasets created from the last session. I'll need to pivot the data so that the variables are columns.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(sf)
library(corrr)
library(car)
library(spdep)
library(zeallot)
library(rstatix)
library(GGally)
library(ggpubr)
library(rcompanion)
source("demographic-functions.R")
```

```{r}
#| warning: false
process <- function(df, var) {
  df %>%
    group_by_at(c("geoid", "district", var)) %>%
    summarise(value = sum(value)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = all_of(var), values_from = value) %>% 
    ungroup()
}

c(abq_age, abq_sex, abq_edu) %<-%
  map2(
    c("age_sex_dist_sf", "age_sex_dist_sf", "edu_dist_sf"),
    c("agegroup", "sex", "education"),
    \(layer, variable) st_read("data/abq_demographics.gpkg", layer = layer) %>%
      process(variable) %>% 
      filter(district != "Los Ranchos")
  )

districts_sf <- st_read("data/abq_demographics.gpkg", 
                        layer = "council_dists") %>% 
  filter(district != "Los Ranchos")
```


# Age Levels

There seemed to be significant variation across council districts, particularly in certain age groups. District 3, in particular, seemed to have many more children and youth, and a lot less older people, who seemed to be more concentrated in District 8. Here are the tables comparing the districts.

![](images/age_dist.png){width="600"}

![](images/edu_dist.png){width="600"}

I will look specifically at people under 20 and over 54. I will calculate the percentage of the population in each district which fall into these groups.

```{r}
under_20_cols <- names(abq_age)[c(4:6, 12, 17)]
cols_gt_55 <- names(abq_age)[13:16]
dist_levels <- unique(abq_age$district) %>% 
  sort()
abq_age <- abq_age %>% 
  mutate(district = factor(district, levels = dist_levels),
         Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric)), na.rm = T),
         Under.20 = rowSums(across(all_of(under_20_cols)), na.rm = T),
         Under.20.pct = Under.20 / Total,
         Over.54 = rowSums(across(all_of(cols_gt_55)), na.rm = T),
         Over.54.pct = Over.54 / Total,
         Under.20 = rowSums(across(all_of(under_20_cols)), na.rm = T))
```

Let's take a look at the kids first. District 3 again seems quite different from the others.

abq_age %>%

```{r}
map_demo_nl <- function(sf, pct = T) {
  dist_plot(council_dists) +
    {
      if (pct) {
        geom_sf(data = sf, aes(fill = percent), alpha = 0.35)
      } else {
        geom_sf(data = sf, aes(fill = value), alpha = 0.35)
      }
    } +
    {
      if (pct) {
        scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::label_percent())
      } else {
        scale_fill_viridis_c(labels = scales::label_comma())
      }
    } +
    geom_sf_label(
      data = council_dists,
      aes(label = district), fontface = "bold",
      nudge_y = 1000, nudge_x = -500, fill = "gray",
      label.padding = unit(0.1, "lines"), size = 3.5
    ) +
    guides(color = "none") +
    labs(
      title = ifelse(pct, "Percentage of the population", "Population"),
      caption = source,
      fill = NULL
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| message: false
abq_age %>% 
  mutate(percent = Under.20.pct) %>% 
  map_demo_nl() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0.1, 0.6),
                       labels = scales::label_percent())
```

```{r}

+

                       labels = scales::label_percent())
```

```{r}
abq_age %>% 
  mutate(percent = Over.54.pct) %>%

```

```{r}
abq_age %>% 
  mutate(percent = Under.20.pct) %>% 
  map_demo_nl() +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(limits = c(0.1, 0.55),
                       labels = scales::label_percent())
```


In order to analyze the variance, the data should be normally distributed. Lets see if this is so.

```{r}
map(list(abq_age$Under.20.pct, abq_age$Over.54.pct),
    \(x) shapiro_test(x))
```

The data is apparently not normally distributed. Let's take a look.

```{r}
plotNormalHistogram(abq_age$Under.20.pct)
ggqqplot(abq_age$Under.20.pct)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
ggqqplot(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
```

Indeed, this isn't normal. The Elfving transformation from the `rcompanion` package can transform this into a normal distribution. The Elfving transformation is qnorm((rank(x) - pi/8)/(N - pi/4 + 1)), where x is the original data, N is the number of observations, and pi is the constant pi. – Sal Mangiafico

```{r}
abq_age$Under.20.pct.ELF <- blom(abq_age$Under.20.pct)
abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF <- blom(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_age$Under.20.pct.ELF)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
```

```{r}
abq_age %>% 
  ggboxplot("district", "Under.20.pct.ELF", fill = "district") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = .1))
abq_age %>% 
  ggboxplot("district", "Over.54.pct.ELF", fill = "district") +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(width = .1))
```

That looks better. Let's test it.

```{r}
map(list(abq_age$Under.20.pct.ELF, abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF),
    \(x) shapiro_test(x))
```

This looks good. Now I'll to the analysis of variance.

```{r}
aov_under_20_pct <- aov(Under.20.pct.ELF ~ district, data = abq_age)
summary(aov_under_20_pct)
aov_over_54_pct <- aov(Over.54.pct.ELF ~ district, data = abq_age)
summary(aov_over_54_pct)
```

The results do show a statistical difference between the districts. Tukey's HSD can show us where.

```{r}
TukeyHSD(aov_under_20_pct)[[1]] %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(`p adj` <= .05)
TukeyHSD(aov_over_54_pct)[[1]] %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(`p adj` <= .05)
```

Indeed, there is a statistically significant different between District 3 and most of the others. Out of curiosity, I will perform the test on the untransformed data.

The Kruskal-Wallis Test uses the following null and alternative hypotheses:

The null hypothesis (H0): The median is equal across all groups.

The alternative hypothesis: (HA): The median is not equal across all groups

```{r}
kruskal.test(Under.20.pct ~ district, data = abq_age)
kruskal.test(Over.54.pct ~ district, data = abq_age)
```

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(ggridges)
plot_dist_ridge <- function(df, var) {
  ggplot(df, aes(
    x = .data[[var]], y = district,
    fill = factor(stat(quantile))
  )) +
    stat_density_ridges(
      geom = "density_ridges_gradient", calc_ecdf = TRUE,
      quantiles = 4, quantile_lines = TRUE, alpha = 0.7,
      jittered_points = TRUE, position = "points_sina"
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Quartiles") +
    theme(axis.title.x = element_blank())
}

map2(list("Under.20.pct", "Over.54.pct"),
     list("Population Percent under 20 years old",
          "Population Percent over 54 years old"),
     \(x, y) abq_age %>% 
       plot_dist_ridge(x) +
       labs(title = y))
```


```{r}
#| warning: false
pairwise.wilcox.test(
  abq_age$Under.20.pct, abq_age$district,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
) %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  filter(p.value <= .05)
pairwise.wilcox.test(
  abq_age$Over.54.pct, abq_age$district,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
) %>% 
  tidy() %>% 
  filter(p.value <= .05)
```


This reveals almost the same results. I should also check for equality of variance.

```{r}
map(list(abq_age$Under.20.pct, abq_age$Over.54.pct,
         abq_age$Under.20.pct.ELF, abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF),
    \(x) bartlett.test(x, abq_age$district))
```

```{r}
# Density plot
ggplot(abq_age, aes(x = Under.20.pct, fill = district)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(title = "Density Plot of Values by Group", x = "Value", y = "Density") +
  theme_minimal()
```


Bartlett's test fails to reject the null hypothesis that all variances are equal. I'll create a linear model to get a sense of the explanatory power of this variable.

```{r}
lm(Under.20.pct.ELF ~ district, data = abq_age) %>% 
  summary()
```

## Older

Again, some of these relationships are significant, but the overall explanatory value is low, with an adusted R-squared of only .114. I'll repeat the analysis for the older age group.

```{r}
shapiro_test(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
```

```{r}
abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF <- blom(abq_age$Over.54.pct)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF)
```

```{r}
abq_age %>% 
  ggboxplot("district", "Over.54.pct.ELF", fill = "district")
```

```{r}
shapiro_test(abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF)
```

```{r}
result <- aov(Over.54.pct.ELF ~ district, data = abq_age)
summary(result)
```

```{r}
TukeyHSD(result)[[1]] %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(`p adj` < .05)
```

There are significant differences here, but fewer.

```{r}
bartlett.test(abq_age$Over.54.pct.ELF, abq_age$district)
```

```{r}
lm(Over.54.pct.ELF ~ district, data = abq_age) %>% 
  summary()
```

As with the other age group, there is correlation, but little explanatory power.

```{r}
kruskal.test(Over.54.pct ~ district, data = abq_age)
```


```{r}
#| warning: false
tmp <- pairwise.wilcox.test(
  abq_age$Over.54.pct, abq_age$district,
  p.adjust.method = "holm"
)
tidy(tmp) %>% 
  filter(p.value <= .05)
```



```{r}
nb <- poly2nb(abq_age, queen = F)
nbw <- nb2listw(nb, style = "W", zero.policy = T)
(gmoran <- moran.test(abq_age$Under.20.pct, 
                      nbw,
                      alternative = "two.sided",
                      na.action = na.omit))
```

The p-value suggest that there is positive spatial autocorrelation.

```{r}
abq_age$Under.20.pct <- if_else(is.na(abq_age$Under.20.pct),
                                0, abq_age$Under.20.pct)
lmoran <- localmoran(abq_age$Under.20.pct, nbw,
                     alternative = "two.sided", na.action = na.omit,
                      zero.policy=attr(nbw, "zero.policy"))

abq_age$lmI <- lmoran[, "Ii"] # local Moran's I
abq_age$lmZ <- lmoran[, "Z.Ii"] # z-scores
abq_age$lmp <- lmoran[, "Pr(z != E(Ii))"]
names(lmoran)
library(tmap)
p1 <- tm_shape(abq_age) +
  tm_polygons(col = "Under.20.pct", title = "vble", style = "quantile") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)

p2 <- tm_shape(abq_age) +
  tm_polygons(col = "lmI", title = "Local Moran's I",
              style = "quantile") +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)

p3 <- tm_shape(abq_age) +
  tm_polygons(col = "lmZ", title = "Z-score",
              breaks = c(-Inf, 1.65, Inf)) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)

p4 <- tm_shape(abq_age) +
  tm_polygons(col = "lmp", title = "p-value",
              breaks = c(-Inf, 0.05, Inf)) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)

tmap_arrange(p1, p2, p3, p4)

```

```{r}
tmap5 <- tm_shape(abq_age) + 
  tm_polygons(col = "lmZ",
              title = "Local Moran's I", 
              style = "fixed",
              breaks = c(-Inf, -1.96, 1.96, Inf),
              labels = c("Negative SAC", "No SAC", "Positive SAC"),
              palette =  c("blue", "white", "red")) +
  tm_layout(legend.outside = TRUE)

# ttm()
tmap5
```

# Education

```{r}
abq_edu <- st_read("data/abq_demographics.gpkg",
                   layer = "edu_dist_sf")

edu_levels <- unique(abq_edu$education)
abq_edu <- abq_edu %>% 
  process("education") %>% 
  filter(district != "Los Ranchos")
```

```{r}
names(abq_edu)
```

```{r}
adv_degree <- names(abq_edu)[c(6, 8, 10)]
col_degree <- c(names(abq_edu)[5], adv_degree)
no_degree <- names(abq_edu)[c(7, 9)]
abq_edu <- abq_edu %>% 
  mutate(district = factor(district, levels = dist_levels),
         Total = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))),
         College.Degree = rowSums(across(all_of(col_degree)), na.rm = T),
         College.Degree.pct = College.Degree / Total,
         Advanced.Degree = rowSums(across(all_of(adv_degree)), na.rm = T),
         Advanced.Degree.pct = Advanced.Degree / Total,
         No.Degree = rowSums(across(all_of(no_degree)), na.rm = T),
         No.Degree.pct = No.Degree / Total)
abq_edu
```

```{r}
shapiro_test(abq_edu$Advanced.Degree.pct)
shapiro_test(abq_edu$College.Degree.pct)
shapiro_test(abq_edu$No.Degree.pct)
```

```{r}
abq_edu$Advanced.Degree.pct.ELF <- blom(abq_edu$Advanced.Degree.pct)
abq_edu$College.Degree.pct.ELF <- blom(abq_edu$College.Degree.pct)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_edu$Advanced.Degree)
shapiro_test(abq_edu$Advanced.Degree.pct.ELF)
```

```{r}
abq_edu$No.Degree.pct.NST <- blom(abq_edu$No.Degree.pct)
plotNormalHistogram(abq_edu$No.Degree.pct)
shapiro_test(abq_edu$No.Degree.pct)
```

```{r}
kruskal.test(Advanced.Degree ~ district, data = abq_edu)
```

  rownames_to_column(var = "rowname") %>% 
  arrange(rowname) %>% 
  filter((str_detect(rowname, "District 3")) |
           str_detect(rowname, "District 8"))
